copies.headline: Adam Is Doing This On Purpose Now
copies.body: The defending champ is 5-0 with a 49-6 all-play, which means Adam hasn't just beaten his schedule, he's beaten everyone's. His 154.5 per game leads the league, his floor is 142.9, and the last three weeks he's gone 142.9, 146.8, 161.8 without appearing to try. The draft grade was 89, T-2nd of 12, and the roster still projects for 133 a week, also first. Kenneth Walker, Purdy, Smith-Njigba questionable or not. Noah gets him in Week 6 at a 126 projection. Good luck.

copies.headline: John's Rams Stack Is Printing Money
copies.body: The 172.7 in Week 5 wasn't a fluke — John's at 134.2 a game, 2nd of 12, with a 37-18 all-play that says 3-2 undersells him by a mile. Luck sits at -0.4, so nothing here is borrowed. The draft graded out at 80, T-9th of 12, which means he's outrunning his own August, mostly by hoarding Los Angeles: Stafford, Kyren Williams and Puka Nacua, plus Brock Bowers and Trey McBride at tight end. Week 6 projects 139 against Logan. Peter's still up 6-3 all-time on him, for now.

copies.headline: Peter's 4-1 Is Doing Some Heavy Lifting
copies.body: Peter's 4-1 looks like a contender until you see the all-play: 28-27, barely over .500, T-5th of 12. He's +1.5 wins over expected, the luckiest mark in the league, and 512.5 points against is the 2nd-fewest — being on the right side of the schedule is a skill right up until it isn't. The draft was real, though, 89 out of 100 and 1st of 12, which is how you get Bijan Robinson and Lamar Jackson on the same team. Then Week 5 happened: 95.4. Kaleb's next, with 108 projected.

copies.headline: Worst Draft Grade, Third-Best Scoring Offense
copies.body: Leif's draft-night roster graded 80, 12th of 12, which means the 131.7 points per game he's averaging — 3rd in the league — is him outrunning the cabin's verdict. The all-play backs it up: 33-22, 60%, also 3rd. Luck is exactly 0.0, so nothing here is borrowed. The wobble is Week 4's 82.8 and a roster projecting 114 a week, 10th of 12. Allen, McCaffrey and Henry don't post 82.8 by accident. Week 6 projects 135 against Grant. Keep the real version showing up.

copies.headline: Christian Is 1-4 And Blameless
copies.body: Nobody in this league has been robbed like Christian. He's averaging 128.4 a game, 4th of 12, with an all-play mark of 31-24 that says he's genuinely good, and he's sitting at 1-4 because he's run into 705.0 points against, 11th-fewest of 12, and a luck figure of -1.8 wins, 12th of 12. The 89 draft grade, tied 2nd, is holding up. Week 5's 103.1 was the first real dud. Lamb and Smith both questionable, Isaac next, 118 projected. It has to break eventually.

copies.headline: CJ's 3-2 Is Mostly Paperwork
copies.body: CJ is 3-2 and the record is the nicest thing about him. The all-play says 28-27, dead even, T-5th of 12, and the luck column says +0.5 wins he didn't actually earn. Last three weeks: 97.9, 114.6, 112.4, a 14-19 all-play stretch that ranks 8th of 12. The roster projects 115 a week, also 8th of 12, which is the problem — Jonathan Taylor and Jalen Hurts are fine, then it's Parker Washington and a questionable Rashee Rice. Week 6 projects 124 against Mitchell. He'll need it.

copies.headline: Mitchell Scores Sixth-Best, Owns Fourth-Worst Record
copies.body: Nobody in this league has been punished harder for showing up. Mitchell is averaging 116.4 a game, 6th of 12, and sits at 1-4 with 644.4 points against — luck of -1.3 wins, 10th-luckiest of 12. The all-play is 25-30, so this isn't a mirage team, just a mugged one. The last three weeks (149.2, 102.5, 132.9) grade out 5th of 12. The problem is the backfield: George Holani, Rachaad White and Najee Harris project for 8, 7 and 5. Nico Collins and Matthew Golden can only do so much.

copies.headline: Grant Is 3-2 On Defense He Doesn't Have
copies.body: Grant is 3-2 because his opponents keep forgetting to show up — 498.4 points against, fewest of 12 — not because he's scoring. The all-play says 21-34, and the last three weeks say 9-24, 27%, dead last of 12 over that stretch. He's +1.1 wins above expected, second-luckiest in the league. The 121.3 in Week 5 was a season high and still only 13 points above his own average. Jacoby Brissett at quarterback projects 15, which tells you everything about the ceiling. Week 6 projects 105 against Leif. Enjoy the cushion, Grant.

copies.headline: Kaleb's 3-2 Is A Magic Trick
copies.body: Kaleb is 3-2 and nothing about that record is earned. The all-play is 21-34, 38%, T-9th of 12, and the luck sits at plus-1.1 wins — T-2nd-luckiest in the league. Scoring 107.7 a game, 10th of 12, will cash eventually. The last three weeks went 132.8, 109.6, 85.7, a tidy little slide ending in the season low. The draft graded 86, T-4th of 12, which makes this worse, not better. Now the roster projects 112 a week, 11th of 12, with 103 coming against Peter. The dress is still available.

copies.headline: Rezac Finally Wins, Roster Still Empty
copies.body: Logan's 1-4 isn't entirely his fault: 736.5 points against is the 12th-fewest of 12, which is a polite way of saying everyone shows up to play him, and his -1.5 luck (11th of 12) confirms he's been scoring fine and losing anyway. The 142.3 in Week 5 was his season high and snapped the skid. The problem is everything after that. This roster projects for 107 a week, 12th of 12, and Week 6 against John comes in at 89. Joe Burrow projects zero. Measure the dress.

copies.headline: The 2-3 Record Is Already Charity
copies.body: Isaac is 2-3 and even that's padded — luck sits at plus-half a win, and the all-play record is 16-39, a 29% clip that ranks 11th of 12. The scoring tells the whole story: 104.0 a game, 11th in the league, with a season high of 121.1 that most teams call a Tuesday. The strange part is the roster projects for about 118 a week, 4th of 12. Javonte Williams, Saquon Barkley, Malik Nabers — that should not produce an 89.3. Christian's up next.

copies.headline: Noah's Cinderella Act Is Four Weeks Late
copies.body: Noah drafted fine — 86 out of 100 on draft night, T-4th of 12 — and has turned it into 100.2 points a game, 12th of 12. The all-play tells the whole story: 14-41, 26%, dead last. He isn't unlucky, he's at -0.3 wins versus expected, which is to say the 1-4 is earned. The 141.3 in Week 5 was the first sign of life, and the roster still projects 115 a week, 9th of 12. Drake Maye, James Cook III, Garrett Wilson — the pieces exist. Week 6 draws Adam. The postseason assassin needs a postseason first.

intro: Adam is 5-0 and it isn't a fluke — 154.5 a game and an 89% all-play mean he'd be beating almost everyone almost every week, luck barely involved at +0.5. Noah holds the basement with 100.2 a game and a 26% all-play, which is a polite way of saying he's lost to the field in three of every four hypothetical matchups. Leif is the week's big jump, #7 to #4 on the back of 131.7 a game, though a 46% form rating says the roster is still arguing with itself. And if you want to split hairs, Grant (42.7) edges Kaleb (42.6) by a tenth for eighth — identical 3-2 records, identical 38% all-play, and Grant's 27% form means that lead is borrowed, not owned.
